articles.title: Near-Ultraviolet and Optical Observations of the White Dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 Reveal Variable Periodicity in its Transiting Debris System
articles.abstract: We observed the transiting debris disk system around the white dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 using the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) in 2025 October, obtaining near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectroscopy with STIS over five consecutive HST orbits. Our abundance analysis supports the accretion of a chondritic body. We complemented our HST program with 16 days of optical time-series photometry beginning in 2025 October, which reveal variable periodicity and rapidly evolving transit morphology. Previous monitoring by TESS during Sectors 4 and 31 confirmed a predominant, stable transit orbital period, $P_{\rm A} = 9.937$ hr, along with a second, transient period, $P_{\rm B} = 11.2$ hr. Our 2025 autumn light curves show transits are dominated by $P_{\rm B} = 11.17$ hr with $P_{\rm A}$ initially appearing as a weaker, secondary feature and eventually returning to predominance. We also identify a candidate transit period of 7.64 hr during the final days of the 2025 autumn campaign, although its significance and persistence remain uncertain. We add simultaneous $ugr$ light curves collected with ULTRACAM in 2024 November that are dominated by $P_{\rm A}$ and show no significant color term. We further compare the transit depths in optical photometry concurrent with our NUV observations, again measuring a lack of transit-dependent extinction except during the fifth HST orbit where a reddening term may arise. The observed variable periodicity and potentially changing color behavior illuminate ongoing dynamical processes, namely collisions, and demonstrate the opportunity for studying dust physics in real time at white dwarf debris disks.

articles.title: The Tierras Observatory: Ultra-Precise Photometry for Characterizing Exoplanets and Their Host Stars
articles.abstract: The Tierras Observatory is a fully robotic 1.3-m telescope at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona. Tierras achieves sub-part-per-thousand (ppt) photometric precision on two timescales: intra-night, to detect and characterize transits of planets around nearby mid-to-late M dwarfs, and night-to-night across an observing season, to characterize the long-term variability of their host stars. We describe the facility and instrument design, our photometric pipeline, and our on-sky performance. We present the first ground-based light curves with sub-ppt precision over timescales of months. This precision enables a range of exoplanet-related science, including the measurement of host star rotation periods, the detection of long-period transits, and the discovery of additional terrestrial planets in known M dwarf systems.

articles.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
articles.abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

articles.title: High-precision abundance analysis of a unique CEMP-no star in Sculptor
articles.abstract: The Carbon-Enhanced Metal-Poor stars (CEMP-no, low barium) are commonly accepted as the direct descendants of Population III (Pop III) stars which either ended their lives as faint supernovae (SNe; E_SN < 10^51 erg) or were fast-rotating stars (spinstars). While CEMP-no stars are common in the Milky Way (MW) and ultra-faint dwarf galaxies (UFDs), they are surprisingly rare in dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs). This could hide an environmental dependence of the properties of Pop III stars, highlighting the importance of high-resolution studies of CEMP-no stars in dSphs. Here we present the first detailed study of a CEMP-no star with [Fe/H] < -3 in the Sculptor dSph. The high-resolution VLT/UVES spectra allowed us to derive one of the most precise abundance patterns obtained for a star belonging to a dwarf galaxy, providing chemical abundances for 17 elements and 4 upper limits. This star, DR20080, is extremely metal-poor, [Fe/H] = -3.26, and clearly enhanced in carbon, [C/Fe] = +1.60 (after correcting for internal mixing). Furthermore, it has low [Ba/Fe] = -1.28. The oxygen abundance of DR20080 ([O/Fe] = +1.53) is significantly higher than the average found in CEMP-no stars in the MW, while the iron-peak elements are under-abundant ([Mn/Fe] = -1.02; [Ni/Fe] = -0.45). The abundance pattern of DR20080 was compared to theoretical yield predictions of Pop III and Pop II SNe to infer the properties of its progenitor. The best result points toward a double Pop III progenitor scenario, with the major contributor to the abundance pattern being a Pop III faint SN with mass m_PopIII = 43 M_0 and explosion energy E_SN = 0.6 x 10^51 erg, while the minor contributor is a Pop III hypernova of m_PopIII = 19.4 M_0 and E_SN = 10 x 10^51 erg. The unique properties of DR20080 have never before been observed in Sculptor or in any other environment within the MW and its satellite system.

articles.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
articles.abstract: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. Detections of H$α$ and Pa$α$ emission from the host galaxy motivate hydrogen recombination seeds, with only indirect support for Ly$α$. A marginal Mg XII feature in the late-time X-ray afterglow provides an event-specific motivation for metal-line seeds, whereas Si XIV, S XVI and iron K-shell transitions are motivated by historical reports of X-ray line features in other gamma-ray bursts. Strong late-time H$_2$ emission detected by the James Webb Space Telescope at the projected burst position motivates our most detailed spectral test. Assuming lateral illumination by the H$_2$ $1-0\,S(1)$ transition at $2.122\,μ{\rm m}$, we calibrate lognormal electron distributions to reproduce the observed MeV photon centroids and widths. We also require IC emission from the ultraviolet (UV) photons driving molecular fluorescence to remain compatible with contemporaneous LAT observations. In a separate test including accompanying molecular transitions, the most favourable configuration, based on the Rh3o photodissociation-region model, approximately describes the MeV feature, although all tested configurations exceed the adopted central spectral references at some energies. For an assumed precursor UV budget, favourable interception substantially reduces the seed-photon energy deficit, but even under ideal excitation and internal escape assumptions, the reference-line photon density in the compact examples falls short of the required value by factors of approximately 4-9. Collisional de-excitation, infrared photon escape and electron cooling impose additional constraints on these configurations. Atomic candidates remain kinematically possible, but their local seed-photon supply is also unestablished.

articles.title: Identification of the C IV $λλ$5801, 5812 Emission in the Off-Nuclear TDE 2025abcr
articles.abstract: TDE 2025abcr is a tidal disruption event (TDE) located approximately 9 kpc in projection from its host galaxy nucleus. Our spectroscopic follow-up with the Very Large Telescope (VLT) reveals C IV $λ\lambda5801, 5812$ emission, representing the first identification of this C IV doublet in a TDE. These transitions are uncommon in active galactic nuclei (AGN) spectra but have been observed in supernova flash spectra and Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars. We propose that the doublet arises from the combined effects of continuum fluorescence and photon trapping in the 312 Å transition, analogous to the mechanism operating in nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) winds. This mechanism requires intense extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) illumination and a high optical depth, providing a distinctive diagnostic of the physical conditions in optically thick TDE outflows. These requirements, together with the relatively narrow widths of the broad emission lines, the presence of Bowen fluorescence features, and the small inferred blackbody radius, favor a compact and dense envelope in TDE 2025abcr. The optical C IV doublet may have been overlooked in previous observational and theoretical studies of TDEs, motivating more detailed radiative-transfer calculations for optically thick outflows. With future TDE samples from Rubin/LSST and WFST, a larger C IV TDE sample will test if this population systematically favors a compact photosphere.

articles.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
articles.abstract: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

articles.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
articles.abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

articles.title: Beyond the Fast Rotators: A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Substellar Weather
articles.abstract: Atmospheric variability provides a unique window into the three-dimensional structure, dynamics, and evolution of brown dwarf and giant exoplanet atmospheres. Recent JWST time-resolved spectroscopic observations have revealed complex wavelength-dependent variability, offering unprecedented insights into cloud structures, thermal perturbations, and atmospheric chemistry. However, existing programs have focused primarily on individual benchmarks and specific scientific questions, resulting in heterogeneous spectral and temporal coverage and leaving important regions of the substellar population underexplored, particularly across a broad range of rotation periods, spectral types, and viewing geometries. A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury program could systematically investigate substellar weather across a diverse, well-characterized population. By combining broad infrared spectroscopic coverage with observations spanning multiple rotations and strategically selected epochs, this program would constrain the contributions of different physical mechanisms while investigating how atmospheric structures depend on rotation, viewing geometry, and fundamental physical properties. Extended monitoring would also improve rotational-period determinations and reveal how atmospheric features evolve from rotation to rotation and over longer timescales. This coordinated effort would provide a consistently designed and uniformly processed dataset of time-resolved spectra and variability diagnostics, enabling population-level comparisons, testing predictions from three-dimensional circulation models, and establishing a framework for interpreting the atmospheric diversity and evolution of brown dwarfs and directly imaged giant exoplanets.

articles.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions
articles.abstract: Water-ice grains are shown to form spontaneously in a cold, weakly-ionized laboratory plasma with trace water admixture when neutrals and ions are cooled below $\sim$200 K. These conditions serve as an analog of ice nucleation in cold astrophysical and atmospheric environments. The ice grains form without the presence of particulate impurities, and do not form in the absence of ionization, indicating that nucleation is induced by ions. Time-resolved ion mass spectrometry provides separate detection of clusters of water molecules on both positive and negative ions. Hydrated negative ions, mainly $\mathrm{OH^-(H_2O)_n}$, grow to $\sim$200 amu, while hydrated positive ions, mainly $\mathrm{H^+(H_2O)_n}$, remain small and short-lived. As the temperature is reduced from room temperature toward 200 K, negative ion clusters grow in size and then drop sharply in abundance, consistent with the onset of rapid growth into macroscopic ice grains below a critical temperature. This indicates that hydrated negative ions are key precursors to ice nucleation in cold, weakly ionized environments, such as the Earth's mesosphere and protoplanetary disks, providing a concrete pathway for ice formation in environments where the nucleation mechanism has remained unresolved. This negative ion pathway is estimated to dominate over ice deposition on pre-existing dust grains in protoplanetary disk locations where there is sufficient UV to partially dissociate water molecules, and in addition, where negative ions such as OH- can form readily through electron attachment at low temperature.

articles.title: Cryohydrologic Flow and Pingo Formation Within Freezing Impact Melts in Occator Crater, Ceres
articles.abstract: Ceres is a volatile-rich dwarf planet in the asteroid belt and a potential relict ocean world. It exhibits surface features indicative of subsurface brine activity, particularly within Occator Crater. High-resolution imagery from NASA's Dawn Mission reveals landslides, gullies, carbonate faculae, and mound-like features resembling terrestrial pingos on the floor of Occator Crater. Some of these landforms have been hypothesized to form from water, either from the ascent of deep crustal brines or from the freezeout of impact melt. Here, we test the hypothesis that pingo-like features can be formed via the freezing of shallow impact melts. We simulate the heat transfer and groundwater flow dynamics of a freezing impact melt deposit on the floor of Occator Crater. We test a comprehensive parameter space of regolith physical and material properties relevant to the cerean environment. We find that impact melt freezinf produces pressure gradients sufficient to drive hydrologic flow within the melt matrix and could transport fluids to the near surface through hydraulic fracturing. For most of the parameter space tested, water volumes delivered to pingo candidates on the surface meet or exceed those likely required for pingo formation. Analogous hydrologic processes may be important in the shallow subsurface of other regions of Occator Crater and Ceres at large as well as other ice-rich planetary bodies.

articles.title: Ejecta fate and deposition in the Didymos-Dimorphos system after the DART impact
articles.abstract: Kinetic impact is a promising technique for asteroid deflection in planetary defense. The NASA Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft collided with Dimorphos, the satellite of the binary asteroid (65803) Didymos, at 6.1449 km s^{-1} in 2022. Observations revealed changes in both the orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos and the heliocentric orbit of the Didymos-Dimorphos system. The ESA Hera spacecraft will arrive at the system at the end of 2026 to investigate the post-impact surfaces. Here, we present an analytical model, based on Maxwell's Z model, to predict ejecta behavior following the DART impact. The model provides the relationships among ejection velocity, ejection angle, and ejecta mass, allowing the momentum enhancement factor beta to be estimated for both Dimorphos and the Didymos-Dimorphos system. We show that the observed beta can be reproduced when 0.3-1% of the impact kinetic energy is converted into ejecta kinetic energy and the effective strength of the target is less than 100 Pa. The escaping mass is estimated to be 0.3-3.0% of the mass of Dimorphos. The globally averaged and minimum ejecta thicknesses on Dimorphos are estimated to be 2.0 m and 0.5 m, respectively, indicating that the entire surface was resurfaced by ejecta deposition, although boulders larger than 1 m were only partially buried. The model also predicts the momentum partition parameter kappa_p to be as low as 0.6, suggesting that the mass and the bulk density of Dimorphos may be revised upward. These predictions provide quantitative constraints for interpreting forthcoming Hera observations.

articles.title: The chemical DNA of the Magellanic Clouds -- VII. The lithium abundance in the Small Magellanic Cloud and the discovery of 4 lithium-rich stars
articles.abstract: Measuring lithium abundance in galaxies beyond the Milky Way (MW) remains a challenging task. In these systems, only stars close to the tip of the red giant branch (RGB) are sufficiently bright to be observed spectroscopically.Their A(Li) are expected to be altered by mixing episodes that occur during the stellar evolution, making the interpretation of measured abundances more complex. In this context, we present A(Li) of 209 RGB stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC),observed with FLAMES@VLT. Approximately one-third of the sample shows a Li line detected at a significance level above 5sigma, while about half of the sample has detections above 3sigma; for the remaining stars, only upper limits can be derived. This sample exhibits a significant star-to-star scatter in A(Li). Using theoretical models, we find that the observed scatter can be likely explained by the combination of 2 effects.First,our stars span a wide range of ages, masses, [Fe/H]. Thermohaline mixing, one of the leading mechanisms proposed to explain the extra mixing occurring at the RGB bump, predicts different levels of A(Li) depletion depending on stellar mass and [Fe/H], naturally contributing to the observed scatter in A(Li). Second, in the SMC, the enrichment in A(Li) driven by novae is expected to occur at lower [Fe/H] than in the MW, because the SMC has experienced a lower star formation efficiency than the MW. This is also supported by the rise of A(Li) with decreasing age, as measured in 3 SMC globular clusters. Furthermore, we report the first identification of 4 low-mass Li-rich giant stars in the SMC, reinforcing the existence of Li-rich stars in extra-galactic systems. All these results demonstrate that A(Li) measured in stars close to the RGB tip, still provide valuable constraints on both stellar/galactic chemical evolution of A(Li) in external galaxies.

articles.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
articles.abstract: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

articles.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
articles.abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

articles.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
articles.abstract: The physical origin of gamma-ray burst (GRB) X-ray flares remains debated, particularly whether they arise from prolonged central-engine activity or from variability in the external shock. Building on our previous analysis of 89 Swift GRBs with measured redshifts, we investigate the rest-frame temporal properties of X-ray flares detected in 61 bursts. We apply a multivariate Gaussian Mixture Model to rest-frame peak times and widths. We identify two statistically distinct populations: early-narrow flares (80%), with characteristic peak times of approximately 10^2 s and w/t_pk <= 1, and late-wide flares (20%), with characteristic peak times of ~ 10^3.5 s and w/t_pk >= 2. Of the 61 single or first flares, 55 belong to the early-narrow population and only 6 to the late-wide population. Of the 36 second flares, 23 (64%) belong to the early-narrow population, with shorter waiting times, whereas 13 (36%) belong to the late-wide population, with substantially longer waiting times. The width-peak-time correlation remains significant for early-narrow flares but not for late-wide flares. Furthermore, we find no correlation between flare width and energy. We find a decline of flare luminosity with peak time, driven primarily by the early-narrow population, but not statistically significant for late-wide flares. These results imply that a simple shift in time, potentially associated with later episodes of central-engine activity, cannot explain the distinction between the two flare populations. On the other hand, the peak times are consistent with expectations from an accretion disk formed following the collapse of a stellar-size massive star. Combined with our previous finding that flare properties are independent of the presence of an X-ray plateau, these results favor prolonged accretion-driven central-engine activity over external-shock variability as the primary origin of X-ray flares.

articles.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
articles.abstract: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges. We model a possible underlying magnetar contribution to the unabsorbed 0.3--10~keV XRT flux over 80--430~s, evolving the spin under fallback-disk and electromagnetic torques. A descriptive estimate gives $P_0\simeq4.25$~ms, $B\simeq3.04\times10^{15}$~G and source-frame $t_{\rm fb}\simeq143$~s, with exploratory temporal-block uncertainty ranges. The effective efficiency reaches its geometry-dependent ceiling of 81.2. At observer time 200~s, this realization has $P_*\simeq4.82$~ms and magnetospheric, corotation and light-cylinder radii $r_{\rm m}\simeq235$~km, $r_{\rm co}\simeq48$~km and $r_{\rm LC}\simeq230$~km. It is on the ejector branch; light-cylinder entry near 255~s initiates negative propeller torque and steepens the decline. The smooth component declines throughout the fitted interval; additional variable emission contributes to the observed maximum near 180~s. A correlated-residual Bayesian analysis permits a fainter component and broader dynamical histories, with median $P_0=16.8$~ms and central 68 per cent interval 2.76--286~ms. However, posterior predictive checks reveal that this statistical description typically underpredicts the observed flux level and variability, limiting its physical interpretation. Fallback-modified magnetar activity remains a possible descriptive scenario, but these analyses do not establish a unique underlying component or robust constraints on the initial spin and disk-interaction history. We also discuss Lense-Thirring precession and alternative mechanisms as possible origins of the early X-ray variability.

articles.title: The PAU Survey: Dissecting strong-lensing systems with narrow-band photometric redshifts
articles.abstract: Wide-field imaging surveys such as Euclid will identify large samples of strong-lens candidates, whose scientific use requires redshifts for both deflectors and lensed sources. Source redshifts are challenging because faint arcs are blended with foreground light. We test lens-model-informed photometry on eight known strong lenses, using broad-band models to define component regions, point-reflection subtraction to reduce contamination, and PAU Survey narrow bands combined with five HSC or CFHT broad bands. BCNz estimates separate lens and source redshift distributions without imposing their expected ordering. All eight lens redshift peaks agree with spectroscopy within $|δ_z|\leq0.014$, where $δ_z=(z_b-z_{\rm spec})/(1+z_{\rm spec})$. Four source peaks, all at $z_{\rm s}^{\rm spec}\leq1.23$, agree within $|δ_z|\leq0.025$. Symmetric subtraction reduces the median source $|δ_z|$ from 0.336 to 0.071. At $|δ_z|<0.05$, narrow- plus broad-band photometry yields eight lens and four source matches, versus three and two using EAZY with broad bands alone. These results demonstrate component redshift recovery in blended systems and support redshift-based lens-candidate assessment alongside morphology and colour. Larger narrow-band surveys, including J-PAS, could extend this approach, pending uncertainty calibration and blind candidate tests.

articles.title: Ångström Exponent Calculation Using Wide-Field Stellar Photometry
articles.abstract: The FRAM (F/Photometric Robotic Atmospheric Monitor) telescopes can measure the aerosol extinction at optical wavelengths using wide-field stellar photometry at the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) sites. The Angstrom exponent describes the wavelength dependence of aerosol extinction. In this work we extend the FRAM method from a single $B$-filter (440 nm) analysis using the Tycho-2 catalogue to a simultaneous three-filter analysis in $B$, $V$, and $R$ (440, 540, and 620 nm) using Gaia DR3 synthetic photometry, which provides photometry directly in the Johnson--Cousins system without passband transformations. The exponent is derived from the vertical aerosol optical depth (VAOD) for the B--V, V--R, and B--R filter pairs at three sites over 2021--2022. The multi-filter VAOD shows a systematic filter-dependent ordering that is inconsistent with physical expectation and produces negative exponents. It is not currently possible to determine which filter yields the correct VAOD, and none of the four processing configurations we tested resolves the ordering. We introduce an intercept correction as a practical remedy that yields physically plausible exponents. At the two southern Paranal sites (CTAO-S0 and CTAO-S1) the exponent distributions are unimodal, with mean $α\approx 0.84$ (B--V) and $0.65$ (B--R) at CTAO-S0 and $0.60$ and $0.41$ at CTAO-S1. At CTAO-N (La Palma) the distributions are bimodal, with $α\approx 0.2$ (B--V) during episodic Saharan dust intrusions and $α\approx 1.3$ under clean background conditions. AERONET sun-photometer measurements on the dates common to both instruments show the same two populations, providing qualitative support for the FRAM method.
